title: AuroraLegal - Hosted API embeddings + rerank demo
summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranking for AuroraLegal search relevance use case; covered API endpoints, Console demo, Optimize suggestions for batching/caching, security notes (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed to run a 2-week pilot dataset benchmark and share security pack + pricing.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off in just a sec. i'm Jordan from Redwood, i run the account.
[00:08] Maya Collins: thanks Jordan, Maya here. excited to see how embeddings + rerank might fix our relevance drift.
[00:15] Priya Shah: hi team, i'm Priya, i'll do the technical walkthrough. quick agenda, quick intro, API demo for embeddings, then a rerank flow, then console + Optimize tips, and q/a.
[00:27] Tom Reyes: sounds good. we get like 30 minutes?
[00:30] Jordan Lee: we have about 40 mins, so we'll be tight but should be fine.
[00:36] Priya Shah: ok starting slide — high level, hosted inference, simplest path is our embeddings endpoint to vectorize documents + queries, then either do simple ANN search and call our rerank endpoint to re-score top candidates.
[00:50] Maya Collins: quick context — our index is about 12M docs, legal precedents and memos, lots of near-duplicates, precision down at top 5. latency target for UI is <200ms 95th. budget is tight, want cost predictable.
[01:06] Priya Shah: got it. two quick product notes — embeddings are small vector calls (cheap), rerank is a classification/regression style call over the top-n hits to compute final relevance. rerank runs on the same hosted models but tuned for reordering rather than generation.
[01:25] Tom Reyes: how many candidates do people usually send to rerank?
[01:29] Priya Shah: typical is 10-50. for latency budget under 200ms we recommend 10-20 with prefix caching and batching. our Optimize tool will suggest an optimal n per query distribution.
[01:42] Jordan Lee: and we can do hybrid routing — cheaper model for embeddings, and a faster/ranked model for rerank, fallback to a quantized variant if capacity is constrained.
[01:53] Maya Collins: security quick Q — all customer data encrypted at rest? and can we bring our KMS?
[01:58] Priya Shah: yes SOC2, encryption at rest and in transit. we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we have KMS integrations for enterprise plans. we also support SSO/SAML and RBAC.
[02:12] Maya Collins: ok good.
[02:15] Priya Shah: demo time — i'll switch to the API explorer. (screen share) calling POST /v1/embeddings with text batch. note the response shape — vector per input. small imperfection in transcript: endpoint in the doc shows /embeds but actual prod is /v1/embeddings, sorry for the typo.
[02:36] Tom Reyes: how do you handle upserts with our existing index? like we already have elastic search + faiss pipeline.
[02:42] Priya Shah: common — you compute embeddings with our API and store vectors in your index (faiss/elasticsearch). then at query time you do ANN to get topK ids, then call our rerank with the original query + candidate doc texts or a short context snippet. that lets rerank use full cross-attention.
[02:58] Maya Collins: cross-attention means slower right?
[03:01] Priya Shah: slightly, but when limited to topK it's fast — rerank is optimized, and we do KV cache and batching. also Optimize can suggest quantized model variants to save tokens and cost.
[03:14] Priya Shah: switching to console — (screen) per-route dashboards, per-model latency, per-token cost. you can see token breakdown and a replay of requests for debugging.
[03:28] Jordan Lee: note, you can pin a model version per environment, run a canary with a subset of queries, and compare relevance metrics in the console.
[03:37] Tom Reyes: can we feed our existing evaluation sets? we have labelled qrels.
[03:41] Priya Shah: absolutely. you can upload eval sets and we run batch evals and surface MRR/NDCG and regression alerts. this is how we detect quality drift after a model change.
[03:52] Maya Collins: latency numbers — what's realistic for rerank of top10?
[03:56] Priya Shah: for top10 on a standard hosted instance we often see 40-120ms p50/p95 depending on model and sequence length. with prefix caching and intelligently batching across queries you can hit your 200ms SLO.
[04:10] Maya Collins: cost? we can't exceed $X per thousand queries — internal constraint (sigh).
[04:16] Jordan Lee: we can model cost in the console; Optimize will recommend smaller models for embeddings and quantized rerank models. we can run a pilot on a representative traffic sample and show cost/latency tradeoff.
[04:30] Priya Shah: moving on to rerank example — i'll send a sample request: POST /v1/rerank with {query:..., candidates:[{id, text}, ...]}. small transcripts note: sometimes our SDK wraps differently, but core API shape is stable.
[04:48] (screen) Priya Shah: here's a real sample, initial ANN returns 20 hits, we pass top10 for rerank, rerank returns score field and explanation tokens. you can also request structured outputs for highlight snippets.
[05:05] Tom Reyes: what about streaming or partial results?
[05:08] Priya Shah: rerank is not streamed typically; embeddings are one-shot. generation endpoints support streaming for chat/generation. rerank returns small JSON so usually fine.
[05:20] Maya Collins: how does caching work? we have a lot of repeated queries.
[05:24] Priya Shah: we have prefix/KV caching for generation endpoints and request-level caching for embeddings. for rerank we support result caching when input candidates and query fingerprint match; Optimize will tell you cache hit expectations.
[05:39] Jordan Lee: question — what about data residency? our legal team needs EU-only storage.
[05:44] Priya Shah: hosted supports region pinning — you can pick EU region and we keep data in-region; for stricter controls we recommend Dedicated or Private where control plane is customer-managed.
[05:58] Maya Collins: ok noted.
[06:00] (brief side conversation about procurement timelines)
[06:20] Lena Ortiz: timeline — we're looking at a pilot in Q4 for 2 weeks, measure effectiveness vs current baseline.
[06:27] Jordan Lee: great — pilot we normally do: sample 5k-20k queries, run both systems, compute NDCG/MRR, cost and latency.
[06:34] Tom Reyes: any code samples for quick POC?
[06:37] Priya Shah: yes i'll share a notebook and a small repo. also a spreadsheet for cost modeling.
[06:43] Jordan Lee: security pack will include SOC2 cert, pen test summary, SSO guide, and KMS integration notes.
[06:50] Maya Collins: can we get a non-prod dataset flow? legal needs assurance we can scrub PII before sending.
[06:55] Priya Shah: yes we recommend anonymization in-stage, or tokenization on client side; we can sign an NDA and advise on best practices.
[07:06] (demo continues showing console graphs and Optimize suggestions)
[07:24] Priya Shah: Optimize suggests lowering rerank top-k to 12, using a quantized L2 rerank model, prefix cache TTL of 30s for repeated queries; estimated cost down 35% with similar MRR in our benchmark sample.
[07:42] Tom Reyes: that sounds promising. is quantization going to affect accuracy?
[07:46] Priya Shah: slight degradation sometimes — that's why we run evals on your qrels. Optimize flags any regression and suggests rollback or different quant profile.
[07:58] Jordan Lee: competitors — often folks compare to OpenAI + custom pipelines, or managed Faiss on GCP / AWS. we also hear teams looking at self-hosted runtimes.
[08:10] Maya Collins: yeah we tried a self-hosted prototype but ops burden killed it.
[08:13] Jordan Lee: recap?
[08:15] Jordan Lee: next steps we'll: share security pack, share a POC notebook + repo, run pilot scope with 10k queries, and provide pricing model.
[08:26] Maya Collins: ok can we get pricing ballpark before the pilot?
[08:29] Jordan Lee: yes we'll send ballpark; final pricing after pilot once we know model choices and qps.
[08:35] (quick Q/A about SLA for hosted)
[08:40] Priya Shah: hosted SLA depends on tier; Dedicated has uptime and latency SLAs.
[08:45] Lena Ortiz: any blockers from our side?
[08:47] Maya Collins: need legal to sign NDA and review security pack, procurement to approve budget.
[08:52] Jordan Lee: noted. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with materials and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[08:58] Tom Reyes: thanks all.
[09:00] (call ends — recording stops)

Note: transcription imperfect in places; some product names mis-heard (e.g., 'redwood dedicate' vs 'Redwood Dedicated'), and timestamps are approximate.
